paragraphs.text: And he entered and was passing through Jericho.
paragraphs.original: Καὶ εἰσελθὼν διήρχετο τὴν Ἰεριχώ.
paragraphs.translit: Kai eiselthōn diērcheto tēn Ierichō.

paragraphs.text: And behold, a man called by name Zacchaeus; and he was a chief publican, and he was rich.
paragraphs.original: καὶ ἰδοὺ ἀνὴρ ὀνόματι καλούμενος Ζακχαῖος, καὶ αὐτὸς ἦν ἀρχιτελώνης καὶ αὐτὸς πλούσιος·
paragraphs.translit: kai idou anēr onomati kaloumenos Zakchaios, kai autos ēn architelōnēs kai autos plousios·

paragraphs.text: And he sought to see Jesus who he was; and could not for the crowd, because he was little of stature.
paragraphs.original: καὶ ἐζήτει ἰδεῖν τὸν Ἰησοῦν τίς ἐστιν, καὶ οὐκ ἠδύνατο ἀπὸ τοῦ ὄχλου ὅτι τῇ ἡλικίᾳ μικρὸς ἦν.
paragraphs.translit: kai ezētei idein ton Iēsoun tis estin, kai ouk ēdynato apo tou ochlou hoti tē hēlikia mikros ēn.

paragraphs.text: And he ran on before, and climbed up into a sycomore tree to see him: for he was to pass that way.
paragraphs.original: καὶ προδραμὼν εἰς τὸ ἔμπροσθεν ἀνέβη ἐπὶ συκομορέαν ἵνα ἴδῃ αὐτόν, ὅτι ἐκείνης ἤμελλεν διέρχεσθαι.
paragraphs.translit: kai prodramōn eis to emprosthen anebē epi sykomorean hina idē auton, hoti ekeinēs ēmellen dierchesthai.

paragraphs.text: And when Jesus came to the place, he looked up, and said unto him, Zacchaeus, make haste, and come down; for to-day I must abide at thy house.
paragraphs.original: καὶ ὡς ἦλθεν ἐπὶ τὸν τόπον, ἀναβλέψας ὁ Ἰησοῦς εἶπεν πρὸς αὐτόν· Ζακχαῖε, σπεύσας κατάβηθι, σήμερον γὰρ ἐν τῷ οἴκῳ σου δεῖ με μεῖναι.
paragraphs.translit: kai hōs ēlthen epi ton topon, anablepsas ho Iēsous eipen pros auton· Zakchaie, speusas katabēthi, sēmeron gar en tō oikō sou dei me meinai.

paragraphs.text: And he made haste, and came down, and received him joyfully.
paragraphs.original: καὶ σπεύσας κατέβη, καὶ ὑπεδέξατο αὐτὸν χαίρων.
paragraphs.translit: kai speusas katebē, kai hypedexato auton chairōn.

paragraphs.text: And when they saw it, they all murmured, saying, He is gone in to lodge with a man that is a sinner.
paragraphs.original: καὶ ἰδόντες πάντες διεγόγγυζον λέγοντες ὅτι Παρὰ ἁμαρτωλῷ ἀνδρὶ εἰσῆλθεν καταλῦσαι.
paragraphs.translit: kai idontes pantes diegongyzon legontes hoti Para hamartōlō andri eisēlthen katalysai.

paragraphs.text: And Zacchaeus stood, and said unto the Lord, Behold, Lord, the half of my goods I give to the poor; and if I have wrongfully exacted aught of any man, I restore fourfold.
paragraphs.original: σταθεὶς δὲ Ζακχαῖος εἶπεν πρὸς τὸν κύριον· Ἰδοὺ τὰ ἡμίσιά μου τῶν ὑπαρχόντων, κύριε, τοῖς πτωχοῖς δίδωμι, καὶ εἴ τινός τι ἐσυκοφάντησα ἀποδίδωμι τετραπλοῦν.
paragraphs.translit: statheis de Zakchaios eipen pros ton kyrion· Idou ta hēmisia mou tōn hyparchontōn, kyrie, tois ptōchois didōmi, kai ei tinos ti esykophantēsa apodidōmi tetraploun.

paragraphs.text: And Jesus said unto him, To-day is salvation come to this house, forasmuch as he also is a son of Abraham.
paragraphs.original: εἶπεν δὲ πρὸς αὐτὸν ὁ Ἰησοῦς ὅτι Σήμερον σωτηρία τῷ οἴκῳ τούτῳ ἐγένετο, καθότι καὶ αὐτὸς υἱὸς Ἀβραάμ ἐστιν·
paragraphs.translit: eipen de pros auton ho Iēsous hoti Sēmeron sōtēria tō oikō toutō egeneto, kathoti kai autos hyios Abraam estin·

paragraphs.text: For the Son of man came to seek and to save that which was lost.
paragraphs.original: ἦλθεν γὰρ ὁ υἱὸς τοῦ ἀνθρώπου ζητῆσαι καὶ σῶσαι τὸ ἀπολωλός.
paragraphs.translit: ēlthen gar ho hyios tou anthrōpou zētēsai kai sōsai to apolōlos.

paragraphs.text: And as they heard these things, he added and spake a parable, because he was nigh to Jerusalem, and [because] they supposed that the kingdom of God was immediately to appear.
paragraphs.original: Ἀκουόντων δὲ αὐτῶν ταῦτα προσθεὶς εἶπεν παραβολὴν διὰ τὸ ἐγγὺς εἶναι Ἰερουσαλὴμ αὐτὸν καὶ δοκεῖν αὐτοὺς ὅτι παραχρῆμα μέλλει ἡ βασιλεία τοῦ θεοῦ ἀναφαίνεσθαι·
paragraphs.translit: Akouontōn de autōn tauta prostheis eipen parabolēn dia to engys einai Ierousalēm auton kai dokein autous hoti parachrēma mellei hē basileia tou theou anaphainesthai·

paragraphs.text: He said therefore, A certain nobleman went into a far country, to receive for himself a kingdom, and to return.
paragraphs.original: εἶπεν οὖν· Ἄνθρωπός τις εὐγενὴς ἐπορεύθη εἰς χώραν μακρὰν λαβεῖν ἑαυτῷ βασιλείαν καὶ ὑποστρέψαι.
paragraphs.translit: eipen oun· Anthrōpos tis eugenēs eporeuthē eis chōran makran labein heautō basileian kai hypostrepsai.

paragraphs.text: And he called ten servants of his, and gave them ten pounds, and said unto them, Trade ye [herewith] till I come.
paragraphs.original: καλέσας δὲ δέκα δούλους ἑαυτοῦ ἔδωκεν αὐτοῖς δέκα μνᾶς καὶ εἶπεν πρὸς αὐτούς· Πραγματεύσασθε ἐν ᾧ ἔρχομαι.
paragraphs.translit: kalesas de deka doulous heautou edōken autois deka mnas kai eipen pros autous· Pragmateusasthe en hō erchomai.

paragraphs.text: But his citizens hated him, and sent an ambassage after him, saying, We will not that this man reign over us.
paragraphs.original: οἱ δὲ πολῖται αὐτοῦ ἐμίσουν αὐτόν, καὶ ἀπέστειλαν πρεσβείαν ὀπίσω αὐτοῦ λέγοντες· Οὐ θέλομεν τοῦτον βασιλεῦσαι ἐφʼ ἡμᾶς.
paragraphs.translit: hoi de politai autou emisoun auton, kai apesteilan presbeian opisō autou legontes· Ou thelomen touton basileusai ephʼ hēmas.

paragraphs.text: And it came to pass, when he was come back again, having received the kingdom, that he commanded these servants, unto whom he had given the money, to be called to him, that he might know what they had gained by trading.
paragraphs.original: καὶ ἐγένετο ἐν τῷ ἐπανελθεῖν αὐτὸν λαβόντα τὴν βασιλείαν καὶ εἶπεν φωνηθῆναι αὐτῷ τοὺς δούλους τούτους οἷς δεδώκει τὸ ἀργύριον, ἵνα γνοῖ τί διεπραγματεύσαντο.
paragraphs.translit: kai egeneto en tō epanelthein auton labonta tēn basileian kai eipen phōnēthēnai autō tous doulous toutous hois dedōkei to argyrion, hina gnoi ti diepragmateusanto.

paragraphs.text: And the first came before him, saying, Lord, thy pound hath made ten pounds more.
paragraphs.original: παρεγένετο δὲ ὁ πρῶτος λέγων· Κύριε, ἡ μνᾶ σου δέκα προσηργάσατο μνᾶς.
paragraphs.translit: paregeneto de ho prōtos legōn· Kyrie, hē mna sou deka prosērgasato mnas.

paragraphs.text: And he said unto him, Well done, thou good servant: because thou wast found faithful in a very little, have thou authority over ten cities.
paragraphs.original: καὶ εἶπεν αὐτῷ· Εὖγε, ἀγαθὲ δοῦλε, ὅτι ἐν ἐλαχίστῳ πιστὸς ἐγένου, ἴσθι ἐξουσίαν ἔχων ἐπάνω δέκα πόλεων.
paragraphs.translit: kai eipen autō· Euge, agathe doule, hoti en elachistō pistos egenou, isthi exousian echōn epanō deka poleōn.

paragraphs.text: And the second came, saying, Thy pound, Lord, hath made five pounds.
paragraphs.original: καὶ ἦλθεν ὁ δεύτερος λέγων· Ἡ μνᾶ σου, κύριε, ἐποίησεν πέντε μνᾶς.
paragraphs.translit: kai ēlthen ho deuteros legōn· Hē mna sou, kyrie, epoiēsen pente mnas.

paragraphs.text: And he said unto him also, Be thou also over five cities.
paragraphs.original: εἶπεν δὲ καὶ τούτῳ· Καὶ σὺ ἐπάνω γίνου πέντε πόλεων.
paragraphs.translit: eipen de kai toutō· Kai sy epanō ginou pente poleōn.

paragraphs.text: And another came, saying, Lord, behold, [here is] thy pound, which I kept laid up in a napkin:
paragraphs.original: καὶ ὁ ἕτερος ἦλθεν λέγων· Κύριε, ἰδοὺ ἡ μνᾶ σου ἣν εἶχον ἀποκειμένην ἐν σουδαρίῳ·
paragraphs.translit: kai ho heteros ēlthen legōn· Kyrie, idou hē mna sou hēn eichon apokeimenēn en soudariō·

paragraphs.text: for I feared thee, because thou art an austere man: thou takest up that which thou layedst not down, and reapest that which thou didst not sow.
paragraphs.original: ἐφοβούμην γάρ σε ὅτι ἄνθρωπος αὐστηρὸς εἶ, αἴρεις ὃ οὐκ ἔθηκας καὶ θερίζεις ὃ οὐκ ἔσπειρας.
paragraphs.translit: ephoboumēn gar se hoti anthrōpos austēros ei, aireis ho ouk ethēkas kai therizeis ho ouk espeiras.

paragraphs.text: He saith unto him, Out of thine own mouth will I judge thee, thou wicked servant. Thou knewest that I am an austere man, taking up that which I laid not down, and reaping that which I did not sow;
paragraphs.original: λέγει αὐτῷ· Ἐκ τοῦ στόματός σου κρίνω σε, πονηρὲ δοῦλε· ᾔδεις ὅτι ἐγὼ ἄνθρωπος αὐστηρός εἰμι, αἴρων ὃ οὐκ ἔθηκα καὶ θερίζων ὃ οὐκ ἔσπειρα;
paragraphs.translit: legei autō· Ek tou stomatos sou krinō se, ponēre doule· ēdeis hoti egō anthrōpos austēros eimi, airōn ho ouk ethēka kai therizōn ho ouk espeira;

paragraphs.text: then wherefore gavest thou not my money into the bank, and I at my coming should have required it with interest?
paragraphs.original: καὶ διὰ τί οὐκ ἔδωκάς μου τὸ ἀργύριον ἐπὶ τράπεζαν; κἀγὼ ἐλθὼν σὺν τόκῳ ἂν αὐτὸ ἔπραξα.
paragraphs.translit: kai dia ti ouk edōkas mou to argyrion epi trapezan; kagō elthōn syn tokō an auto epraxa.

paragraphs.text: And he said unto them that stood by, Take away from him the pound, and give it unto him that hath the ten pounds.
paragraphs.original: καὶ τοῖς παρεστῶσιν εἶπεν· Ἄρατε ἀπʼ αὐτοῦ τὴν μνᾶν καὶ δότε τῷ τὰς δέκα μνᾶς ἔχοντι—
paragraphs.translit: kai tois parestōsin eipen· Arate apʼ autou tēn mnan kai dote tō tas deka mnas echonti—

paragraphs.text: And they said unto him, Lord, he hath ten pounds.
paragraphs.original: καὶ εἶπαν αὐτῷ· Κύριε, ἔχει δέκα μνᾶς—
paragraphs.translit: kai eipan autō· Kyrie, echei deka mnas—

paragraphs.text: I say unto you, that unto every one that hath shall be given; but from him that hath not, even that which he hath shall be taken away from him.
paragraphs.original: λέγω ὑμῖν ὅτι παντὶ τῷ ἔχοντι δοθήσεται, ἀπὸ δὲ τοῦ μὴ ἔχοντος καὶ ὃ ἔχει ἀρθήσεται.
paragraphs.translit: legō hymin hoti panti tō echonti dothēsetai, apo de tou mē echontos kai ho echei arthēsetai.

paragraphs.text: But these mine enemies, that would not that I should reign over them, bring hither, and slay them before me.
paragraphs.original: πλὴν τοὺς ἐχθρούς μου τούτους τοὺς μὴ θελήσαντάς με βασιλεῦσαι ἐπʼ αὐτοὺς ἀγάγετε ὧδε καὶ κατασφάξατε αὐτοὺς ἔμπροσθέν μου.
paragraphs.translit: plēn tous echthrous mou toutous tous mē thelēsantas me basileusai epʼ autous agagete hōde kai katasphaxate autous emprosthen mou.

paragraphs.text: And when he had thus spoken, he went on before, going up to Jerusalem.
paragraphs.original: Καὶ εἰπὼν ταῦτα ἐπορεύετο ἔμπροσθεν ἀναβαίνων εἰς Ἱεροσόλυμα.
paragraphs.translit: Kai eipōn tauta eporeueto emprosthen anabainōn eis Hierosolyma.

paragraphs.text: And it came to pass, when he drew nigh unto Bethphage and Bethany, at the mount that is called Olivet, he sent two of the disciples,
paragraphs.original: Καὶ ἐγένετο ὡς ἤγγισεν εἰς Βηθφαγὴ καὶ Βηθανίαν πρὸς τὸ ὄρος τὸ καλούμενον Ἐλαιῶν, ἀπέστειλεν δύο τῶν μαθητῶν
paragraphs.translit: Kai egeneto hōs ēngisen eis Bēthphagē kai Bēthanian pros to oros to kaloumenon Elaiōn, apesteilen dyo tōn mathētōn

paragraphs.text: saying, Go your way into the village over against [you]; in which as ye enter ye shall find a colt tied, whereon no man ever yet sat: loose him, and bring him.
paragraphs.original: λέγων· Ὑπάγετε εἰς τὴν κατέναντι κώμην, ἐν ᾗ εἰσπορευόμενοι εὑρήσετε πῶλον δεδεμένον, ἐφʼ ὃν οὐδεὶς πώποτε ἀνθρώπων ἐκάθισεν, καὶ λύσαντες αὐτὸν ἀγάγετε.
paragraphs.translit: legōn· Hypagete eis tēn katenanti kōmēn, en hē eisporeuomenoi heurēsete pōlon dedemenon, ephʼ hon oudeis pōpote anthrōpōn ekathisen, kai lysantes auton agagete.

paragraphs.text: And if any one ask you, Why do ye loose him? thus shall ye say, The Lord hath need of him.
paragraphs.original: καὶ ἐάν τις ὑμᾶς ἐρωτᾷ· Διὰ τί λύετε; οὕτως ἐρεῖτε ὅτι Ὁ κύριος αὐτοῦ χρείαν ἔχει.
paragraphs.translit: kai ean tis hymas erōta· Dia ti lyete; houtōs ereite hoti Ho kyrios autou chreian echei.

paragraphs.text: And they that were sent went away, and found even as he had said unto them.
paragraphs.original: ἀπελθόντες δὲ οἱ ἀπεσταλμένοι εὗρον καθὼς εἶπεν αὐτοῖς.
paragraphs.translit: apelthontes de hoi apestalmenoi heuron kathōs eipen autois.

paragraphs.text: And as they were loosing the colt, the owners thereof said unto them, Why loose ye the colt?
paragraphs.original: λυόντων δὲ αὐτῶν τὸν πῶλον εἶπαν οἱ κύριοι αὐτοῦ πρὸς αὐτούς· Τί λύετε τὸν πῶλον;
paragraphs.translit: lyontōn de autōn ton pōlon eipan hoi kyrioi autou pros autous· Ti lyete ton pōlon;

paragraphs.text: And they said, The Lord hath need of him.
paragraphs.original: οἱ δὲ εἶπαν ὅτι Ὁ κύριος αὐτοῦ χρείαν ἔχει.
paragraphs.translit: hoi de eipan hoti Ho kyrios autou chreian echei.

paragraphs.text: And they brought him to Jesus: and they threw their garments upon the colt, and set Jesus thereon.
paragraphs.original: καὶ ἤγαγον αὐτὸν πρὸς τὸν Ἰησοῦν, καὶ ἐπιρίψαντες αὐτῶν τὰ ἱμάτια ἐπὶ τὸν πῶλον ἐπεβίβασαν τὸν Ἰησοῦν·
paragraphs.translit: kai ēgagon auton pros ton Iēsoun, kai epiripsantes autōn ta himatia epi ton pōlon epebibasan ton Iēsoun·

paragraphs.text: And as he went, they spread their garments in the way.
paragraphs.original: πορευομένου δὲ αὐτοῦ ὑπεστρώννυον τὰ ἱμάτια ἑαυτῶν ἐν τῇ ὁδῷ.
paragraphs.translit: poreuomenou de autou hypestrōnnyon ta himatia heautōn en tē hodō.

paragraphs.text: And as he was now drawing nigh, [even] at the descent of the mount of Olives, the whole multitude of the disciples began to rejoice and praise God with a loud voice for all the mighty works which they had seen;
paragraphs.original: ἐγγίζοντος δὲ αὐτοῦ ἤδη πρὸς τῇ καταβάσει τοῦ Ὄρους τῶν Ἐλαιῶν ἤρξαντο ἅπαν τὸ πλῆθος τῶν μαθητῶν χαίροντες αἰνεῖν τὸν θεὸν φωνῇ μεγάλῃ περὶ πασῶν ὧν εἶδον δυνάμεων,
paragraphs.translit: engizontos de autou ēdē pros tē katabasei tou Orous tōn Elaiōn ērxanto hapan to plēthos tōn mathētōn chairontes ainein ton theon phōnē megalē peri pasōn hōn eidon dynameōn,

paragraphs.text: saying, Blessed [is] the King that cometh in the name of the Lord: peace in heaven, and glory in the highest.
paragraphs.original: λέγοντες· Εὐλογημένος ὁ ἐρχόμενος βασιλεὺς ἐν ὀνόματι κυρίου· ἐν οὐρανῷ εἰρήνη καὶ δόξα ἐν ὑψίστοις.
paragraphs.translit: legontes· Eulogēmenos ho erchomenos basileus en onomati kyriou· en ouranō eirēnē kai doxa en hypsistois.

paragraphs.text: And some of the Pharisees from the multitude said unto him, Teacher, rebuke thy disciples.
paragraphs.original: καί τινες τῶν Φαρισαίων ἀπὸ τοῦ ὄχλου εἶπαν πρὸς αὐτόν· Διδάσκαλε, ἐπιτίμησον τοῖς μαθηταῖς σου.
paragraphs.translit: kai tines tōn Pharisaiōn apo tou ochlou eipan pros auton· Didaskale, epitimēson tois mathētais sou.

paragraphs.text: And he answered and said, I tell you that, if these shall hold their peace, the stones will cry out.
paragraphs.original: καὶ ἀποκριθεὶς εἶπεν· Λέγω ὑμῖν, ὅτι ἐὰν οὗτοι σιωπήσουσιν, οἱ λίθοι κράξουσιν.
paragraphs.translit: kai apokritheis eipen· Legō hymin, hoti ean houtoi siōpēsousin, hoi lithoi kraxousin.

paragraphs.text: And when he drew nigh, he saw the city and wept over it,
paragraphs.original: Καὶ ὡς ἤγγισεν, ἰδὼν τὴν πόλιν ἔκλαυσεν ἐπʼ αὐτήν,
paragraphs.translit: Kai hōs ēngisen, idōn tēn polin eklausen epʼ autēn,

paragraphs.text: saying, If thou hadst known in this day, even thou, the things which belong unto peace! but now they are hid from thine eyes.
paragraphs.original: λέγων ὅτι Εἰ ἔγνως ἐν τῇ ἡμέρᾳ ταύτῃ καὶ σὺ τὰ πρὸς εἰρήνην— νῦν δὲ ἐκρύβη ἀπὸ ὀφθαλμῶν σου.
paragraphs.translit: legōn hoti Ei egnōs en tē hēmera tautē kai sy ta pros eirēnēn— nyn de ekrybē apo ophthalmōn sou.

paragraphs.text: For the days shall come upon thee, when thine enemies shall cast up a bank about thee, and compass thee round, and keep thee in on every side,
paragraphs.original: ὅτι ἥξουσιν ἡμέραι ἐπὶ σὲ καὶ παρεμβαλοῦσιν οἱ ἐχθροί σου χάρακά σοι καὶ περικυκλώσουσίν σε καὶ συνέξουσίν σε πάντοθεν,
paragraphs.translit: hoti hēxousin hēmerai epi se kai parembalousin hoi echthroi sou charaka soi kai perikyklōsousin se kai synexousin se pantothen,

paragraphs.text: and shall dash thee to the ground, and thy children within thee; and they shall not leave in thee one stone upon another; because thou knewest not the time of thy visitation.
paragraphs.original: καὶ ἐδαφιοῦσίν σε καὶ τὰ τέκνα σου ἐν σοί, καὶ οὐκ ἀφήσουσιν λίθον ἐπὶ λίθον ἐν σοί, ἀνθʼ ὧν οὐκ ἔγνως τὸν καιρὸν τῆς ἐπισκοπῆς σου.
paragraphs.translit: kai edaphiousin se kai ta tekna sou en soi, kai ouk aphēsousin lithon epi lithon en soi, anthʼ hōn ouk egnōs ton kairon tēs episkopēs sou.

paragraphs.text: And he entered into the temple, and began to cast out them that sold,
paragraphs.original: Καὶ εἰσελθὼν εἰς τὸ ἱερὸν ἤρξατο ἐκβάλλειν τοὺς πωλοῦντας,
paragraphs.translit: Kai eiselthōn eis to hieron ērxato ekballein tous pōlountas,

paragraphs.text: saying unto them, It is written, And my house shall be a house of prayer: but ye have made it a den of robbers.
paragraphs.original: λέγων αὐτοῖς· Γέγραπται· Καὶ ἔσται ὁ οἶκός μου οἶκος προσευχῆς, ὑμεῖς δὲ αὐτὸν ἐποιήσατε σπήλαιον λῃστῶν.
paragraphs.translit: legōn autois· Gegraptai· Kai estai ho oikos mou oikos proseuchēs, hymeis de auton epoiēsate spēlaion lēstōn.

paragraphs.text: And he was teaching daily in the temple. But the chief priests and the scribes and the principal men of the people sought to destroy him:
paragraphs.original: Καὶ ἦν διδάσκων τὸ καθʼ ἡμέραν ἐν τῷ ἱερῷ· οἱ δὲ ἀρχιερεῖς καὶ οἱ γραμματεῖς ἐζήτουν αὐτὸν ἀπολέσαι καὶ οἱ πρῶτοι τοῦ λαοῦ,
paragraphs.translit: Kai ēn didaskōn to kathʼ hēmeran en tō hierō· hoi de archiereis kai hoi grammateis ezētoun auton apolesai kai hoi prōtoi tou laou,

paragraphs.text: and they could not find what they might do; for the people all hung upon him, listening.
paragraphs.original: καὶ οὐχ εὕρισκον τὸ τί ποιήσωσιν, ὁ λαὸς γὰρ ἅπας ἐξεκρέματο αὐτοῦ ἀκούων.
paragraphs.translit: kai ouch heuriskon to ti poiēsōsin, ho laos gar hapas exekremato autou akouōn.
